title: Motion in a Plane
seo_title: Motion in a Plane Class 11 Physics Worksheet with Answers (NCERT Chapter 3)
standard_code: Class 11 Physics, Chapter 3: Motion in a Plane
standard_text: Scalar and vector quantities, position and displacement vectors, general vectors and notation, equality of vectors, multiplication of vectors by a real number, addition and subtraction of vectors, unit vectors, resolution of a vector, rectangular components, motion in a plane, projectile motion, uniform circular motion.
meta_desc: Free CBSE Class 11 Physics worksheets for NCERT Chapter 3 Motion in a Plane: vectors, resolution, projectile motion (height, time and range), relative velocity and uniform circular motion. 100 questions with answers.
key_big: Treat horizontal and vertical motion separately.
key_sub: R = u² sin 2θ/g; H = u² sin²θ/2g; a = v²/r.
body_html:
How to think about it

Vectors add by the triangle or parallelogram law and can be resolved into components A cos θ and A sin θ. Two perpendicular vectors give a resultant √(a² + b²). In projectile motion the horizontal velocity u cos θ stays constant while the vertical motion has acceleration g.

Time of flight T = 2u sin θ/g, maximum height H = u² sin²θ/(2g) and range R = u² sin 2θ/g, greatest at 45°. In uniform circular motion speed is constant but the acceleration v²/r = ω²r points to the centre.

Example

u = 20 m/s, θ = 45°. Range?

400 × 1 ÷ 9.8

Answer: 40.8 m

Example

3 N and 4 N at right angles?

√(9 + 16)

Answer: 5 N

Common mistakes

  • Using sin θ instead of sin 2θ for the range.
  • Thinking velocity is zero at the top of a projectile.
  • Calling uniform circular motion unaccelerated.
